written: 2026-10-31, after T_COPULA_JOINT_DEV_RESULT_20261031.md and before any result of a state-conditional marginal.
disclosure: motivated by results already seen on the same development databases and samples: the static own_trajectory marginal (one error distribution for every row of a cell) gives single-event O/E of 0.5-1.15 across samples and databases (map < 65 and bicarbonate < 18 overpredicted), and the online Mondrian MultiQT marginal of ONLINE_JOINT_DEV_RESULT_20261031.md improved but did not fix them. The state-conditional form tested here is the static day-one part of that same frozen form (v2 quintile scale with the amended recording-resolution floor, tail8 Mondrian categories), without the online updates. In-sample for the motivation; only an unused external lockbox is independent evidence.
question: Does a state-conditional (Mondrian, scale-normalized) static marginal calibrate single threshold events better than the unconditional static marginal, without worsening the multivariate forecast under the Gaussian dependence layer?

marginal.unconditional: point + empirical quantile of the cell's signed errors on MIMIC conformal patients (as own_trajectory_joint_dev_rule_20261031.json)
marginal.mondrian: point + s(x) * empirical quantile of the normalized signed errors e / s(x) of the MIMIC conformal patients in the row's category. s = v2 quintile scale of |e| fitted on MIMIC selection patients (osler_jepa.interval_scale, scheme quintile), floored at the recording resolution of the cell's MIMIC calibration current values (threshold_event_form.resolution; online_joint_dev_rule_amendment_20261031.json). Categories = tail8 bins of the current value (osler_jepa.predictive_distribution.value_bins on the MIMIC calibration current values); a category with < 30 conformal patients uses the pooled conformal scores.

joint.correlation: as own_trajectory_joint_dev_rule_20261031.json, shared by both marginals (estimated on the raw signed errors of MIMIC selection patients; disclosed: not re-estimated on the normalized scores, so that the two systems differ only in the marginal)
joint.coupling: the same latent draws map through each marginal's quantile function

events: map < 65, heart_rate > 120, potassium >= 6.0, bicarbonate < 18, creatinine rise >= 0.3, glucose > 180 (joint_forecast_dev.EVENTS); probability = share of the 50 members (levels (k - 0.5) / 50) in the event
calibrated_band: single-event O/E in [0.8, 1.25] (defined here for this readout)

primary_readouts.single_event: per test database x event x horizon, on all labelled test rows of the cell, with >= 30 events in a sample: mondrian closer than unconditional in that sample if |log O/E| is smaller; robustly closer if closer in >= 80% of the samples where it is scored
primary_readouts.multivariate: per test database and block: energy score of mondrian+gaussian vs unconditional+gaussian, patient-cluster bootstrap 95% CI of the difference; worse in a sample if the lower bound > 0; robustly worse if worse in >= 80% of 5 samples

decision: mondrian replaces unconditional as the marginal under the dependence layer only if (a) it is robustly closer on at least half of the database x event x horizon combinations scored in >= 4 samples, and (b) its energy score is not robustly worse on any database x block. AGENTS.md changes only with user approval.
secondary_readouts: share of combinations inside the calibrated band in >= 80% of samples, per marginal
central 90% tail exceedance per cell: share of rows below q0.05 and above q0.95 (target 0.05 each)
variogram score of mondrian+gaussian vs unconditional+gaussian and vs mondrian+independent
same-horizon joint-event O/E (joint_forecast_dev.EVENT_PAIRS, >= 30 joint events) for both marginals under both copulas
